STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are 20-30 cm. This plate looks medium-large, around 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the bacon strips are about 12-13 cm long. The plate spans roughly two bacon lengths across, so about 24-26 cm. Both cues agree.
Final width: 25 cm square, area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg: covers roughly 35-40% of the plate, footprint about 0.38 x 625 = 240 cm². It is a loose layer about 1 cm thick on average (a mound, so roughly half its peak of ~2 cm). Volume ≈ 240 x 1.0 = 240 ml. Density 0.8 g/ml gives about 190 g.
- Bacon: three visible pieces (two full strips and one smaller broken piece). Each full strip is about 10-12 g cooked, the broken piece about 4 g. Total about 25 g. Pieces are thin and flat, so no hidden layer.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The egg is a single layer over the plate with no base under it, and nothing sits beneath the bacon. No extra items.

STEP 5 - Energy values (cooked):
- Scrambled egg (with some butter/oil): about 150 kcal per 100 g.
- Cooked bacon: about 540 kcal per 100 g.

Totals: egg 190 g → about 285 kcal; bacon 25 g → about 135 kcal. Total about 420 kcal, total weight about 215 g.
